A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExpRAG and DischargeQA. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original DischargeQA experiments with four LLMs, retrieval comparisons, weighting and top-k ablations, and a clinical case study.

after.justification: Section 5 and the appendices retain original experiments and add Qwen3 results, embedding-ranker comparisons, patient-similarity correlations, and biomedical-model findings.

M1.justification: The weighted Jaccard ranking over diagnosis, medication, and procedure codes, followed by report selection and text retrieval, remains unchanged. Auto-merging is named more prominently in v2 but was already the default retriever in v1.

E1.justification: Both use the same MIMIC-derived DischargeQA coverage: 436 diagnosis, 444 medication, and 400 instruction questions. Additional backbones and ranking diagnostics evaluate existing tasks and retrieval components within the same clinical cohort.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the central text-ranker comparison by adding all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2 alongside the original text baseline, now identified as bge-small-en-v1.5. Tables 3 and 4 compare these rankers against ExpRAG on QA and intrinsic retrieval quality.

E3.justification: V2 adds a ranking-evaluation protocol with 100 target patients and 100 candidates each, including 20 randomly sampled and 80 with nonzero EHR similarity, GPT-4o-mini annotations, and Pearson/Spearman metrics. It also adds Qwen3 and Baichuan configurations. Existing QA metrics, equal similarity weights, and default k=15 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new correlation analysis directly examines whether patient rankings align with annotated clinical similarity. Appendix A.5.3 adds analyses of Baichuan's invalid responses and UltraMedical-70B's context-length failures. Original weighting, top-k, retriever, and clinical-case analyses remain; relocating the latter material does not constitute new evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's new correlation coefficients serve as retrieval evaluation metrics rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds Qwen3, additional ranker, correlation, and Baichuan results. It also changes retained Table 2 entries: Mistral's ExpRAG medication F1 changes from 0.353 to 0.371, and Deepseek's ExpRAG medication accuracy from 1.13% to 0.90%. Original weighting, top-k, and retriever-ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical content. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden DischargeQA's stated purpose to evaluating other EHR-based RAG systems and medical agents, and extend the comparison claim to multiple text-based rankers. The principal method and dataset contributions and the headline 5.2% relative-improvement claim remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive applicability boundaries involving confusion between target and retrieved patients in Baichuan and context overflow preventing reliable UltraMedical-70B evaluation. It also interprets the new correlations as evidence of more faithful retrieval and expands the rationale for preserving complete patient reports. These extend v1's more limited discussion of failure conditions.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the previously unspecified baseline encoder, discloses the instruction-filter threshold of at least four bullet points, specifies Qwen3's thinking mode, and details candidate sampling and annotation for ranking evaluation. These substantially improve documentation; they do not establish changes to the existing ExpRAG procedure. Code/data access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Sentence-BERT, C-Pack/BGE, and Qwen3, supporting the expanded experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning around clinical experience retrieval remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands explanatory appendices on dataset construction and ranking workflows, reorganizes backbone descriptions, and condenses the main clinical case study while moving its details to Appendix A.8. The retriever analysis also moves to the appendix. These are substantive narrative changes despite extensive retention of the main method text.

P2.justification: V2 adds workflow Figures 5–6 and comparison Tables 3, 4, and 8, restructures and highlights Table 2, and reformats the clinical-case figure. It also adds auto-merging to Figure 3 and relocates the unchanged retriever table. The original discharge-note example and prompt remain as renumbered figures.

improvement.justification: Expanded ranker comparisons, direct retrieval evaluation, clearer setup documentation, and biomedical-model failure disclosures improve evidence and transparency. The gains are qualified: similarity validation relies on LLM annotations, and Section 5.1 still calls GPT-4o best across tasks although new Table 2 gives Qwen3 higher instruction accuracy, 95.3% versus 91.3%. Overall, v2 is better supported but retains consequential interpretation problems.
